claims.claim_text: A nontrivial binary upcycle exists with n=12,d=3,L=512; it answers Question 9.2 affirmatively.
The 512 windows partition all 4096 binary 12-words into sets of eight completions.
128 octal digits specify the complete cycle.
The window length 12 does not divide cycle length 512.
Chen, Kitaev, Mütze and Sun introduced universal partial words and cyclic versions.
Fillmore et al. Theorem 3.1 gives binary n=8,d=1 examples.
Fillmore et al. Question 9.2 asks whether upcycles with d>1 exist.
Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2 multiply alphabet size while preserving n,d.
Corollary 8.14 requires d=n/4 for nontrivial period-four frames.
Carey et al. Definition 8.2 permits several cyclic words in a universal partial quasi-family.
The four displayed rows have 128 octal digits and decode to the accepted word.
Digits 0,1,7 decode to wildcard000, wildcard001, wildcard111.
Completion sets are disjoint iff ordinary unequal symbols occur at a common offset.
The cycle has 512 positions with wildcards precisely at indices zero modulo four, also cyclically.
Every window has three wildcards and nine ordinary symbols, with no repeated physical position.
Each completion set has exactly eight members.
All 130816 pairs have an ordinary conflict; every test succeeds.
Pairwise disjoint completion sets have union cardinality 512*8=4096=2^12.
The direct loop checks all 4096 total words at all 512 starts without sampling.
Eleven starts 501 through 511 wrap around and are included.
The program performs 2097152 compatibility tests and prints the stated counts.
The direct check counts starting indices, with shared characters read from one decoded word and exact integer counts.
FGKMM26 raises n not dividing cycle length immediately after Question 9.2.
FGKMM26 has authors Fillmore, Goeckner, Kirsch, Martin, McGinnis; DCC 94 article152 (2026), DOI10.1007/s10623-026-01841-x.
CKKP25 has authors Carey, Kearney, Kirsch, Popescu; DCC93 pp2803-2822 (2025), DOI10.1007/s10623-025-01609-9.
CKMS17 has authors Chen, Kitaev, Mütze, Sun; DMTCS19(1) paper16 (2017), DOI10.23638/DMTCS-19-1-16.

excluded: Definitions, questions, and methodology descriptions (including discovery and AI disclosure) excluded under citation-check extraction rules. Repeated claims grouped by ID; no charts or quantitative plots.
